title: Size dependence of microstructure of AlSi10Mg alloy fabricated by selective laser melting

nodes.label: SLM is used for thin walls and lattice struts, so a sub-millimetre feature must be known to behave like the bulk block it is designed from
How the microstructure and hardness of SLM AlSi10Mg change as the built feature shrinks below a millimetre has not been measured systematically
A thinner plate sees a different thermal history during the build, so its solidification and solid-state structure, and with them its hardness, should differ from a centimetre-sized one
AlSi10Mg powder, measured composition Al-10.8Si-0.2Mg-0.4Fe wt%
Eleven plate samples with specified widths from 0.1 to 10 mm built side by side on one base plate
Use a CALPHAD equilibrium calculation of the Si phase fraction as the reference against which the measured Si fraction is read
Selective laser melting at 380 W with 30 um layers, 150 um hatch spacing and 67 deg layer rotation under argon
Every width shows the same stacked melt-pool structure, pools about 150 um high and 300 um wide; the 0.27 mm plate is barely one pool wide and has a wavy, powder-decorated surface
Elongated alpha-Al grains grow with <001> along the build direction, and the {001}, {011} and {111} area fractions (about 20, 15 and 8%) do not change with plate width
The mean intercept length of the high-angle boundaries stays near 7 um at every plate width
The density of low-angle boundaries falls from 0.149 to 0.125 um-1 as the plate width falls from 10.41 to 0.27 mm

attrs.image_note: read from the three EBSD maps in the upper half of the packet's F7 image file; those maps carry no offered panel id, so this node cites F7 at figure level

nodes.label: In wide plates the Si particles line the cell boundaries; below about 1 mm they are increasingly found inside the columnar alpha-Al cells
The measured Si fraction stays below the CALPHAD equilibrium value in every sample, and the shortfall narrows as the plate gets thinner, so less Si stays in supersaturated solution
Hardness falls slightly with plate width, from about 112 Hv at 10 mm to about 107 Hv at 0.28 mm
A thin plate is reheated more by the neighbouring tracks and cools more slowly overall, so Si precipitates out of the supersaturated alpha-Al during the build and the low-angle boundaries recover

attrs.mechanism_class: in-process ageing by intrinsic heat treatment

nodes.label: Texture and grain size are set by the melt pool and are size-independent, but the Si precipitation state and the low-angle boundary density, and with them the hardness, depend on the built width
Below about 0.4 mm the SLM route reaches its dimensional limit, and a sub-millimetre feature should not be assumed to carry the hardness of the bulk block
The hardness difference is about 5 Hv against error bars of 3-4 Hv, so the size effect on hardness is at the edge of the measurement scatter
Optical sections show overlapping arc-shaped melt pools in all four widths; in the thinnest plate a single column of pools spans the whole width between two wavy, particle-decorated surfaces

attrs.image_note: pool height about 100-150 um and width 200-300 um measured against the 100 um bar in panel (d)

nodes.label: The orientation maps are dominated by red, Z-elongated grains in every width, with equiaxed grains at the pool boundaries and a few coarse edge grains on the thin plates

attrs.image_note: a 5 um step against the stated 10 um mean grain width leaves only about two measurement points across a grain

nodes.label: The {001}, {011} and {111} area fractions scatter around 0.20, 0.15 and 0.08 with no drift over two decades of plate width
The mean intercept length sits between 6.9 and 7.8 um at every width, with the thinnest plates marginally the coarsest

nodes.label: The fine-step maps carry printed low-angle boundary densities of 0.149, 0.143 and 0.125 um-1 for the 10.41, 2.10 and 0.27 mm plates

nodes.label: The equilibrium Si (diamond) fraction of the measured composition is 10.5% below the solidus
Hardness runs from 111.8 Hv at 10.4 mm down to 106.6 Hv at 0.27 mm under a 0.98 N load
The error bars of the widest and narrowest samples overlap, and the trend is not monotonic: the 0.35 and 0.42 mm plates read about 109.3 Hv, above the 0.5-0.66 mm plates at about 107.5 Hv

nodes.label: CALPHAD equilibrium calculation of the Al-Si-Mg-Fe system with the PanAl database
Quantitative microscopy relation Sv = 2/L between boundary area per unit volume and mean intercept length
SLM AlSi10Mg annealed at elevated temperature develops the same intragranular Si morphology
The EOS material data sheet and earlier studies put the dimensional limit of this SLM route near 0.4 mm

notes: A size-sweep paper with no performance stage: the spine ends at hardness and the conclusion. Two structure branches run in parallel, one that does NOT change with width (melt pools, texture, grain size) and one that does (low-angle boundaries, Si precipitation state); the MEC node explains only the second. Lost: the sample geometry and dimensional-accuracy figure (F1), the CALPHAD figure (F2, not opened, so the 10.5% equilibrium fraction enters as a text-backed computed OBS), and the schematic (F9, tier C, no panels offered). Record defects: the packet holds 9 image files for a paper with 11 figures; packet F7 is a single image file containing BOTH paper Fig. 7 (fine-step EBSD maps) and paper Fig. 8 (SEM of the Si particles), and the panel store offers only four ids for its seven panels, and all four are crops of the SEM panels of paper Fig. 8 (F7a = 10.41 mm, F7b = 2.10 mm, F7c = 0.66 mm, F7d = 0.27 mm); the three EBSD maps of paper Fig. 7 have no offered id and are cited at figure level; packet F8 is paper Fig. 9; paper Fig. 10 (Si number density and area fraction against width) is absent, so the central quantitative support for the Si-fraction claim (h13) had to enter as a text-only OBS. The F8 panel cue lines misread the panel titles 'dm = 10.41 mm' etc. as scale bars. Image findings: the hardness error bars of the widest and narrowest plates overlap and the trend is non-monotonic (i11); every plotted intercept length is below the 8 um quoted in the text and is only about 1.5 times the 5 um EBSD step (i4); the SEM contrast differs between the wide-plate and thin-plate panels, so Si area fractions should not be compared by eye (i6).

review.audit_summary: 2 audits (h18 the 5 Hv effect against 3-4 Hv bars, i11 the overlapping bars and non-monotonic trend). Both bear directly on h14, the terminal property claim of a paper with no performance stage, and both are stated as scatter rather than as refutation, which is the right distinction here. i4's note that every plotted intercept is below the text's 8 um and only about 1.5x the 5 um EBSD step is carried inside the evidence node rather than as a separate audit, which is correct under the audit budget.
